deploy-bot: deploy-check prevented promotion of release/2026-03-21 -> prod: model_variant_map.json differs between staging and prod (routing/capacity parity). See /checks/7901

anika: pinging infra — what's the exact diff?

carlos: quick diff: staging model_variant_map.json maps `text-gen-xl` -> `variant: rwd-4-xl-quant, gpu_type: t4`, prod maps `text-gen-xl` -> `variant: rwd-4-xl-quant, gpu_type: a100`. File path: infra/configs/model_variant_map.json

ravi: that's a big one. If the variant expects a100 on prod but staging used t4, performance/latency assumptions will be wrong and autoscaler math could break.

anika: why did staging have t4? I recall PR #5249 added a cheap fallback for dev-stage experiments.

carlos: yes, PR #5249 changed default `gpu_type` for non-prod bundles to `t4` to save cost, but the variant mapping in staging was updated too. Deploy-bot flagged because the prod mapping still expects `a100`.

release-manager: change window until 23:00 UTC. We need a quick decision: 1) pin the release to prod mapping (so promoted bundle uses prod model_variant_map) 2) hotpatch prod mapping to match staging (requires infra approval + capacity check) 3) rollback staging image to match prod mapping. Thoughts?

ravi: pinning is safest. It avoids touching prod capacity and keeps behavior identical to current prod. Hotpatching prod could oversubscribe A100 capacity if scheduling expects a100 but we suddenly request t4 — actually reverse: staging used t4, prod expects a100; hotpatching prod to t4 would reduce resource needs but must ensure no tenant requires a100.

anika: we should also consider tenant-level overrides. Some large tenants are pinned to a100 variants explicitly. If we pin to prod mapping we're fine. If we change prod mapping to t4 we may break those tenants.

sre-bot: runbook check: allowed mitigation is to set `configOverrides.modelVariantMapSha` in release values to the prod SHA. Risk: low. Steps: 1) open override PR that sets `configOverrides.modelVariantMapSha: <prod-sha>` in `charts/models/values.release.yaml` 2) run `ci/release-promote --env prod --verify` 3) monitor GPU scheduling metrics and tail inference error logs for 15m. If issues revert PR.

carlos: grabbing prod manifest SHA now: prod: d4f6a7b8c9e0f1a2b3c4, staging: e9f0d1c2b3a4f5e6d7c8.

anika: i'll open the override PR to pin to prod mapping and tag infra + release.

(anika pasted): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5199 — override `configOverrides.modelVariantMapSha: d4f6a7b8c9e0f1a2b3c4`

release-manager: LGTM. Approving once CI finishes. We'll also add a note in release docs that variant mapping diverged and a follow-up compatibility audit is scheduled.

sre-bot: CI passed for PR 5199. Promotion queued. Monitoring hooks enabled.

carlos: promoting now. watching scheduler logs and pod evictions.

sre-bot: Promotion finished. No pod evictions, GPU allocation stable. No increase in latency.

anika: created ISSUE-1312 to run the compatibility audit and reconcile staging/prod mapping rules. Link: https://tracker.redwood.ai/ISSUE-1312

ravi: also adding a small CI check to warn on `gpu_type` differences between envs during preflight.

release-manager: thanks team. Closing thread but follow-ups are scheduled in ISSUE-1312 and infra PR 5199. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: thread archived.
